AWAKENED_DYNASTY.bonus_to_hit_when_led.quoted_text: While a NECRONS CHARACTER model is leading this unit, each time a model in this unit makes an attack, add 1 to the Hit roll.
AWAKENED_DYNASTY.bonus_to_hit_when_led.trigger: attacker's unit is being led by a friendly CHARACTER â€” approximated as: (a) at least one alive friendly CHARACTER is within its own aura_range of the attacker, AND (b) that CHARACTER's LeaderAbility.host_keys lists the attacker's UNIT_CATALOG key (i.e. the attachment is legal in 10e per the leader datasheet's Bodyguard list). The host-key gate prevents the +1 from firing on units that cannot be led (C'tan Shards, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Doomstalkers, Wraiths, Tomb Blades, Scarab Swarms, etc.).

_comment: Rule citations for every 10e mechanic the simulator implements. CLAUDE.md Â§10 mandates an entry here for any Detachment flag set True, any LeaderAbility, any simulator-side gate, or any Stratagem effect. scripts/audit_rules.py walks the code and verifies every rule-bearing flag has an entry.

_schema.quoted_text: Verbatim from the source â€” include the trigger half.
_schema.rule_name: Short name the rule is known by in the codex.
_schema.scope: army-wide / unit-led / character-only / phase-gated / keyword-gated / weapon-keyword

simulator.acts_of_faith.effect: Gain 1 Miracle die at the start of each battle round (while at least one Sororitas unit is alive), plus 1 each time a friendly Sororitas codex-unit is fully destroyed (last sim-instance of that profile.name dies, non-TRANSPORT only, while at least one other Sororitas unit is still alive). Each die is a pre-rolled D6 banked in a pool (soft cap 8, no hard codex limit). Before any d6 roll a unit may perform one Act of Faith per phase, substituting one banked die for ONE d6 of that roll. Only substitutes when the swap converts fail -> success (simulator greedy heuristic). Two budget paths: legacy (SWEG_AOF_PER_PHASE unset/0) collapses to one per codex-unit per round (conservative); per-phase path (SWEG_AOF_PER_PHASE=1) enforces one per phase per codex-unit, resetting at the start of the Shooting phase and again at the start of the Fight phase.
simulator.acts_of_faith.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is Adepta Sororitas, each unit from your army with this ability can perform one Act of Faith per phase. This is done using Miracle dice. GAINING MIRACLE DICE If your Army Faction is Adepta Sororitas, you gain 1 Miracle dice: - At the start of each battle round. - Each time an Adepta Sororitas unit from your army is destroyed. Each time you gain a Miracle dice, roll one D6. The number you roll is the value of that Miracle dice. This value cannot be changed or re-rolled, unless a rule specifically states otherwise. Keep your Miracle dice to one side â€“ this is your Miracle dice pool. PERFORMING AN ACT OF FAITH Before making a dice roll for a model or unit from your army with the Acts of Faith ability, if you have one or more dice in your Miracle dice pool, that unit can perform an Act of Faith. If it does, select one of the dice from your Miracle dice pool to substitute that dice roll (if a roll involves more than one dice, e.g. a Charge roll or Battle-shock test, only a single dice can be substituted). The dice that is being substituted is not rolled; instead the value of the selected Miracle dice is used as if it had been rolled (this counts as an unmodified dice roll of that value for all rules purposes). Each Miracle dice can only be selected for substitution once. Once all Miracle dice substitutions have been made, remove the chosen Miracle dice from your Miracle dice pool, and roll all remaining, unsubstituted dice that are a part of the dice roll. You can use Miracle dice when a unit performs an Act of Faith for any of the following types of dice roll: Advance roll, Battle-shock test, Charge roll, Damage roll, Hit roll, Saving throw, Wound roll.
simulator.acts_of_faith.trigger: attacker / defender unit has Adepta Sororitas faction tag AND its army has at least one Miracle die banked AND the natural d6 roll (hit / wound / save) would fail AND the codex-unit (profile.name group) has not already used its Acts of Faith budget this phase (per-phase path, SWEG_AOF_PER_PHASE=1) or this round (legacy path); the simulator greedy heuristic only substitutes when a banked die flips fail -> success. SOROR-AOF-PER-PHASE (wave 238): gate SWEG_AOF_PER_PHASE (default OFF) implements the codex-correct one-Act-of-Faith-per-phase rule; when ON, each Sororitas unit may spend once in the Shooting phase AND once in the Fight phase per round. The historical reason for the conservative per-round cap (SOROR-DIAG-3 +14.39 pt over-performance) has been attributed to the broken invulnerable-save mapper (fixed, commit 299aefc). Legacy path remains byte-identical when gate is OFF. Squad-level cap: all sim instances sharing a profile.name count as one codex unit, enforcing the per-squad-not-per-model constraint. APPROXIMATION (retroactive substitution): the codex requires declaring the substitution BEFORE the roll; the simulator substitutes retroactively only on failures (equivalent in expectation under optimal play, noted per CLAUDE.md section 10). SOROR-DETACHMENT-V1 on-death generation fix: the previous code fired one die per sim-instance destroyed (e.g. 25 dice for 25 Repentia Squad instances), over-generating by ~4.65x. Fixed to fire only when the LAST alive sim-instance of a given profile.name dies (the codex unit is fully destroyed), and excluding TRANSPORT units which do not carry the Acts of Faith ability on their datasheets. TRANSPORT gate: Sororitas Immolator / Sororitas Rhino / Repressor are VEHICLE TRANSPORT datasheets and do not list the Acts of Faith ability; their destruction does not award Miracle dice.

simulator.basket_best_ranged_per_model.effect: When _collect_weapons_for_model yields multiple fixed ranged weapons for one model type, only the single best (by expected_damage_through_baseline) non-[PISTOL] weapon is kept. This prevents the Autopistol/Bolt pistol secondary from diluting the basket average of the model's primary weapon in _flatten_to_basket. Pistol-only models are unaffected.
simulator.basket_best_ranged_per_model.quoted_text: Select one ranged weapon that model is equipped with and make attacks with it. … [PISTOL]: … each time a model makes an attack with this weapon, if the attacking unit is within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units, that attack can only target one of those enemy units.
simulator.basket_best_ranged_per_model.rule_name: Shooting Phase — one ranged weapon per model
simulator.basket_best_ranged_per_model.trigger: Any time the heterogeneous-squad mapper collects fixed ranged weapons for a single model type and the model carries more than one fixed ranged weapon (e.g. Mining laser + Autopistol, Plasma incinerator + Bolt pistol). A model will always elect to fire its highest-damage weapon in the Shooting phase; the Autopistol/Bolt pistol secondary is only usable during the Fight phase under the [PISTOL] rule.

simulator.basket_fraction_gating.effect: Unit.attack gates LANCE / DEVASTATING WOUNDS / ANTI-X consumption per shot via a Bernoulli draw against a basket-weight fraction recorded by the mapper. For heterogeneous squads (Rubric Marines, Skyweavers, Beast Snagga Boyz, AdMech Skitarii) the MAP-3 boolean UNION marks the keyword present on the synthetic average weapon so the picker is aware of it; this fraction then ensures each shot only fires the keyword with probability equal to the proportion of basket weight whose underlying weapon legitimately carries it. Single-weapon units default to fraction 1.0 (keyword fires for every shot) so the legacy gate is preserved. Rule-correct: each MODEL in a squad shoots its OWN weapon and squad attacks come from the mixed pool of those weapons; we don't track per-model weapon assignments so the random-expectation Bernoulli matches the real per-attack distribution.
simulator.basket_fraction_gating.quoted_text: Each time a unit shoots, after selecting targets, the player commanding that unit allocates each weapon in that unit at one of those target units. If a model has more than one ranged weapon, it can split its attacks between different targets, but if it does, all of the attacks from each weapon must be made against the same target.
simulator.basket_fraction_gating.rule_name: The Shooting Phase / Select Targets (per-weapon attack allocation)
simulator.basket_fraction_gating.trigger: squad's chosen primary weapon is a synthetic basket-average (BSData mapper heterogeneous path) AND the primary carries at least one of LANCE / DEVASTATING WOUNDS / ANTI-X via the MAP-3 union of basket weapons; per-shot Bernoulli draw against the recorded basket fraction decides whether the keyword fires for that shot

simulator.beacons_of_rage.effect: +1 to the Hit roll; additionally +1 to the Wound roll when the target is Below Half-strength (current_health < profile.health / 2)
simulator.beacons_of_rage.quoted_text: While a friendly World Eaters unit is within 6" of this unit, each time a model in that unit makes a melee attack that targets a unit (excluding Monsters and Vehicles), add 1 to the Hit roll. If that attack targets a unit that is Below Half-strength, add 1 to the Wound roll as well.
simulator.beacons_of_rage.trigger: attacker is a World Eaters unit; a friendly Eightbound or Exalted Eightbound unit is alive (sim does not track 6" aura ranges precisely, see leaders.effective_buffs for the same approximation); attack is melee; target lacks MONSTER and VEHICLE keywords

simulator.benefits_of_cover.effect: +1 to the armour save (one pip better; cover never improves a save by more than 1). AP0 / 3+-save exception applied to ALL models (not just INFANTRY): a model with a Save characteristic of 3+ or better gets NO Benefit of Cover against an attack whose Armour Penetration is 0; it still gains the +1 save against any attack with AP. The universal 2+ armour-save floor still applies. Melee attacks ignore cover entirely. The stale 9th-edition terrain -1-to-hit and the 'INFANTRY cap at 3+' approximation have been removed.
simulator.benefits_of_cover.quoted_text: Until the end of the phase, each time a ranged attack is allocated to a model in this unit while it is receiving the Benefit of Cover, add 1 to the armour saving throw made against that attack. If a model has a Save characteristic of 3+ or better, that model cannot have the Benefit of Cover against attacks made with weapons that have an Armour Penetration characteristic of 0.
simulator.benefits_of_cover.trigger: ranged attack resolves against a defender whose `in_cover` flag is set (inside terrain that grants cover, or the army's blanket cover flag); precision against CHARACTER and Ignores Cover bypass this; the AP0 / 3+-save exception suppresses cover when the attack's AP is 0 and the target's base Save is 3+ or better

simulator.big_guns_never_tire.effect: permitted to shoot; -1 to all hit rolls this activation
simulator.big_guns_never_tire.quoted_text: While a VEHICLE or MONSTER unit is within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units, it can shoot, but it suffers -1 to its Hit rolls while doing so.
simulator.big_guns_never_tire.trigger: attacker has VEHICLE or MONSTER keyword AND is within 1" of an enemy

simulator.blessings_of_khorne.effect: each activated Blessing applies army-wide to WORLD EATERS units until end of battle round; modelled: Martial Excellence -> melee SUSTAINED HITS 1; Warp Blades -> melee LETHAL HITS; Cleaving Blows -> melee AP+1
simulator.blessings_of_khorne.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is WORLD EATERS, at the start of the battle round, you can make a Blessings of Khorne roll. To do so, roll eight D6. You can then use those dice to activate up to two Blessings of Khorne. Each Blessing of Khorne specifies the dice results it requires (where a number is specified, a double or triple of that value or higher is required). You can only activate each Blessing of Khorne once per battle round. Any unused dice from the Blessings of Khorne roll are then discarded. Once activated, each Blessing of Khorne applies to all units from your army with this ability until the end of the battle round. Modelled Blessings: "Martial Excellence" (Double 4+ or Triple 1+): "Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability." "Warp Blades" (Double 5+ or Triple 2+): "Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [LETHAL HITS] ability." "Cleaving Blows" (Double 6+): "Improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of melee weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1."
simulator.blessings_of_khorne.trigger: start of each battle round; WORLD EATERS army rolls 8D6 and may activate up to two Blessings whose dice thresholds are met

simulator.blood_surge.effect: the Berzerker unit makes a free reactive move of D6+2 inches toward the closest enemy unit, finishing as close as possible to it (clamped to engagement range 1" if it can reach)
simulator.blood_surge.quoted_text: In your opponent's Shooting phase, each time an enemy unit has shot, if any models from this unit were destroyed as a result of those attacks, this unit can make a Blood Surge move. To do so, roll one D6 and add 2 to the roll: models in this unit move a number of inches up to this result, but this unit must finish that move as close as possible to the closest enemy unit.
simulator.blood_surge.trigger: defender is a World Eaters Khorne Berzerkers unit; an enemy unit has shot at it during the opponent's Shooting phase; one or more models were destroyed as a result of those attacks; in per-model representation (one Unit instance per physical model, squad grouped by squad_id) this is detected as an alive-to-dead transition on the targeted Unit instance, and the whole surviving squad surges together
simulator.blood_surge.implementation_note: wave 237 Issue #61: prior implementation used a pooled-health formula (wounds_per_model = profile.health / profile.min_models) which produced wounds_per_model = 0.2 for a 2-wound model in a 10-model squad, triggering Blood Surge on any chip damage. The fix detects model destruction via the alive-to-dead health transition on the targeted Unit instance, consistent with the per-model architecture where each Unit IS one physical model.

simulator.charge_end_base_to_base.effect: Gated SWEG_CHARGE_BASEEDGE (default ON since wave 240 — adopted with SWEG_DEPLOY_COLLISION as the collision pair on the metric-neutral N=80 paired confirm: gated mean absolute error 5.08 -> 5.13, in-band factions 5/22 -> 8/22, seed-5 live overlap incidents 217 -> 53, cross-army overlaps 49 -> 2; set =0 to restore the legacy centre-distance placement). On a successful charge the charger's end POSITION is computed so its BASE EDGE finishes within 1.0" of the target's base edge (centre distance = 1.0 + attacker_base_radius + target_base_radius), not so its CENTRE is 1.0" from the target's centre. The legacy centre-to-centre placement drove the charger 2-3" inside a big-based target's base. The base-edge spot is validated against the no-overlap collision predicate (_collision_pos_legal, allow_engagement=True) so the charger never ends on top of another model; if the straight approach spot is illegal it is sought deterministically around the target centre at the same base-edge distance (fixed +/-10-degree steps out to +/-90 degrees, nearest-first); if no legal spot exists it falls back to the legacy placement so a successful charge is never cancelled. No random numbers are consumed; the gate-off path is byte-identical to the legacy placement.
simulator.charge_end_base_to_base.quoted_text: Within Engagement Range of every unit that you selected as a target of the charge. When measuring the distance between models, measure between the closest points of the bases of the models you're measuring to and from. While a model is within 1" horizontally and 5" vertically of an enemy model, those models - and their units - are within Engagement Range of each other.
simulator.charge_end_base_to_base.rule_name: Charge Move / Engagement Range / Measuring Distances
simulator.charge_end_base_to_base.trigger: Charge phase; a charging unit's 2D6 charge roll succeeds; the gate SWEG_CHARGE_BASEEDGE is set; the charger's end position is placed so its base edge is within 1" of the target's base edge instead of its centre 1" from the target's centre.

simulator.combat_drugs.effect: one Combat Drug is active army-wide on every WYCH CULT unit until the start of the next Command phase; the drugs are mutually exclusive when picked manually (the same drug cannot be reselected in the same battle). SwegHammer applies Adrenalight (+1 melee Attacks on every WYCH CULT model) as the canonical single army-wide pick for Round 1 only; the other five drugs (Hypex, Serpentin, Painbringer, Grave Lotus, Splintermind) are not modelled. DRK-DIAG-4 corrected the prior implementation, which had stacked four drugs simultaneously across four different WYCH CULT units (rules-illegal). DRK-NON-SKYSPLINTER-V1 (2026-05-29) corrected the per-round timing: drug was previously applied at battle start and persisted for the entire battle (5 rounds), giving Adrenalight x5 the codex magnitude. The fix moves application to the Command phase and clears the drug at each round-start, so Adrenalight fires for Round 1 only (matching the codex "cannot reselect" restriction). Rounds 2-5 have no active drug (no other drugs wired).
simulator.combat_drugs.quoted_text: At the start of your Command phase, select which Combat Drugs will be active for your army until the start of your next Command phase. To do so, either select one from the list below (you cannot select the same Combat Drug more than once per battle), or randomly select two by rolling two D6. Adrenalight: Add 1 to the Attacks characteristic of melee weapons equipped by WYCH CULT models. Hypex: Add 2" to the Move characteristic of WYCH CULT models. Serpentin: Improve the Weapon Skill characteristic of melee weapons equipped by WYCH CULT models by 1. Painbringer: Add 1 to the Toughness characteristic of WYCH CULT models. Grave Lotus: Add 1 to the Strength characteristic of melee weapons equipped by WYCH CULT models. Splintermind: Improve the Leadership characteristic of WYCH CULT models by 1, and improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of ranged weapons equipped by WYCH CULT models by 1.
simulator.combat_drugs.trigger: Drukhari army; one Combat Drug active army-wide at a time on every WYCH CULT unit

simulator.dark_pacts.approximation_note: Player choice [LETHAL HITS] vs [SUSTAINED HITS 1] collapsed to always-Lethal Hits (dominant pick against high-toughness targets; no target-context plumbing)
simulator.dark_pacts.effect: elected unit gains transient_lethal_hits ([LETHAL HITS]) for the phase; on failed 2D6>=Ld test the unit suffers D3 mortal wounds. CHOICE COLLAPSE: [SUSTAINED HITS 1] option not modelled — always grants [LETHAL HITS].
simulator.dark_pacts.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is Heretic Astartes, each time a unit with this ability is selected to shoot or fight, it can make a Dark Pact. If it does, it must first take a Leadership test before any effects of the Dark Pact are resolved; if that test is failed, that unit suffers D3 mortal wounds. Then, select one of the following abilities for that unit's weapons to gain until the end of the phase: [LETHAL HITS] / [SUSTAINED HITS 1]
simulator.dark_pacts.trigger: attacker unit faction is Chaos Space Marines AND is selected to shoot or fight AND is the highest-DPA unit in the army this round AND DPA >= 6

simulator.fights_first_chargers.effect: Within the active player's Fight phase pass (`_run_round_vanilla_turns`), units that charged this turn (uid in `_charging_this_round`) fight before units that did not. Implemented as a stable sort with key `0 if charging else 1` so non-charger relative order is preserved.
simulator.fights_first_chargers.quoted_text: All eligible units that have the FIGHTS FIRST ability must fight in the Fights First step. Then, in the Remaining Combats step, all other eligible units fight. Each time you select an eligible unit from your army to fight with that made a Charge move this turn, that unit fights first.
simulator.fights_first_chargers.trigger: active player's Fight phase pass; chargers (units with uid in `_charging_this_round`) are sorted ahead of non-chargers before the per-unit `_do_fight` loop. Datasheet-level FIGHTS FIRST keyword is handled separately via `simulator.fights_first_keyword`.

simulator.fights_first_keyword.effect: Within the active player's Fight phase pass (`_run_round_vanilla_turns`), units whose UnitProfile has `fights_first=True` are tiered into the Fights First step alongside chargers (sort key 0), ahead of remaining combats (sort key 1). The flag is set by the BSData mapper's `extract_fights_first` from a 'Fights First' infoLink / inline profile / 'FIGHTS FIRST' prose mention on the datasheet entry.
simulator.fights_first_keyword.quoted_text: All eligible units that have the FIGHTS FIRST ability must fight in the Fights First step. Then, in the Remaining Combats step, all other eligible units fight.
simulator.fights_first_keyword.rule_name: Fight phase — Fights First step (datasheet keyword)
simulator.fights_first_keyword.trigger: active player's Fight phase pass; units with `profile.fights_first=True` (parsed by BSData mapper from datasheets like Wyches, Howling Banshees, Custodian Wardens, Mandrakes) are sorted into tier 0 alongside chargers via `_fight_priority` before the per-unit `_do_fight` loop.

simulator.fnp_in_threat_score.effect: AI threat heuristic multiplies effective durability by 1 / (1 - (7-fnp)/6); fnp=7 (no FNP) is the no-op. Does NOT change combat math (Unit.attack still rolls actual FNP per receive_damage); only fixes opponent target selection.
simulator.fnp_in_threat_score.quoted_text: Some models have 'Feel No Pain' listed in their abilities. This is followed by a value in brackets. Each time a model with this ability would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds the value in brackets, that wound is not lost. This is known as a Feel No Pain roll.
simulator.fnp_in_threat_score.trigger: AI threat-score heuristic in `code/strategy.py._durability` evaluates how attractive a defender is as a melee target â€” folds the defender's resolved Feel No Pain value (lower of profile.fnp and any leader-aura / detachment / stratagem-granted FNP via leaders.effective_buffs) into the durability denominator so opponent AIs correctly read Death Guard Plague Marines (5+), Custodian Wardens (under Auric Mortalis 5+), Tyranid Tervigon (5+), Nurgle daemons (5+), Typhus-led Plague Marines (Destroyer Hive 5+), and Drukhari with Pain Tokens (6+) as harder targets.

simulator.multi_profile_weapon_selection.effect: Unit.attack ranged branch computes expected net damage under BOTH primary and secondary profiles against the current target at the current distance (accounting for range gating and target wounds bounding excess-damage waste) and swaps to the secondary stat block via dataclasses.replace when its expected damage is higher; primary remains the default when no secondary is recorded or when primary's expected damage wins
simulator.multi_profile_weapon_selection.quoted_text: Each time a unit shoots, after selecting targets, the player commanding that unit allocates each weapon in that unit at one of those target units. If a model has more than one ranged weapon, it can split its attacks between different targets, but if it does, all of the attacks from each weapon must be made against the same target.
simulator.multi_profile_weapon_selection.trigger: datasheet carries TWO distinct ranged weapon profiles (Stormsurge Pulse Driver 72" vs Pulse Blastcannon-focused 18", Magnus the Red Gaze of Magnus vs Tzeentch's Firestorm, etc.); the bsdata mapper records the runner-up as `secondary_*` on UnitProfile when present

simulator.pistol_exclusivity.effect: unit fires the Pistol set OR the non-Pistol set, not both
simulator.pistol_exclusivity.quoted_text: A model armed with one or more Pistols can either shoot with all of its Pistols or with all of its other ranged weapons. Choose which it will do each time it shoots.
simulator.pistol_exclusivity.trigger: a unit shooting in its Shooting phase that owns both Pistol and non-Pistol ranged weapons

simulator.primary_vp_no_round_1.effect: Primary VP scored only from battle round 2 onward; round 1 scores 0 primary VP
simulator.primary_vp_no_round_1.quoted_text: At the end of the Command phase, each player scores Victory Points for the primary objectives they control. Note that the Command phase in the first battle round does not score primary Victory Points.
simulator.primary_vp_no_round_1.trigger: end of Command phase, rounds 2-5 only (not round 1)

simulator.rend_and_tear.effect: +1 to the Damage characteristic of that attack
simulator.rend_and_tear.quoted_text: Each time a model in this unit makes a melee attack that targets a Monster or Vehicle unit, until the end of the phase, improve the Damage characteristic of that attack by 1.
simulator.rend_and_tear.trigger: attacker is the World Eaters Exalted Eightbound unit; attack is melee; target has MONSTER or VEHICLE keyword

simulator.resolute_will.effect: -1 to the Wound roll (subject to the Â±1 modifier cap in Unit.attack)
simulator.resolute_will.quoted_text: While a CHARACTER is leading this unit, each time an attack targets this unit, if the Strength characteristic of that attack is greater than the Toughness characteristic of this unit, subtract 1 from the Wound roll.
simulator.resolute_will.trigger: defender has `resolute_will` set on the UnitProfile (per overrides.json), defender is actually led â€” leaders.is_actually_led() returns True (at least one in-range friendly CHARACTER whose LeaderAbility.host_keys lists the defender's UNIT_CATALOG key), AND the attack's Strength characteristic is strictly greater than the defender's Toughness characteristic

simulator.secondary_selection.effect: Only the picked 2 Fixed Secondaries (+ chosen Tactical cards) score VP for that army. `score_round_delta` / `score_position_delta` zero any component absent from `chosen_secondaries`. Previously all four Fixed + both Tactical scored every round for every army, asymmetrically over-rewarding balanced kill-heavy / mobile rosters.
simulator.secondary_selection.quoted_text: Before deployment, each player must either select two different Fixed Secondary Missions from the four below, or use the Tactical Secondary Missions deck. Each player scores Victory Points from their two chosen Fixed Secondary Missions throughout the battle, or draws from the Tactical Secondary Missions deck each battle round.
simulator.secondary_selection.trigger: battle start; `code/secondaries.py::pick_secondaries(own_army, enemy_army)` selects 2 Fixed (bring_it_down / cull_the_horde / assassination — no_prisoners is Tactical-only in CA-2025-26 tournament play) + 2 Tactical (engage_on_all_fronts / behind_enemy_lines) per army by a deterministic heuristic on enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE count and own FLY/MOUNT count; persisted on `Army.chosen_secondaries`

simulator.squad_size_durability_factor.effect: AI threat heuristic multiplies effective durability by a squad-size factor (lone model 1.0; 2-model squad 1.05; 5-model 1.20; 10-model 1.45; 20-model 1.95). This is an AI design heuristic, NOT a 10e rule â€” the cited core wording motivates why per-attack allocation makes high-model-count squads structurally harder to remove than 1-vs-1 durability suggests. Does NOT change combat math; only fixes opponent target selection.
simulator.squad_size_durability_factor.quoted_text: If one or more models in the target unit have already lost one or more wounds, or have already had attacks allocated to them this phase, the attack must be allocated to one of those models. Otherwise, the player commanding the target unit chooses which model in their unit the attack is allocated to.
simulator.squad_size_durability_factor.trigger: AI threat-score heuristic in `code/strategy.py._durability` â€” paired compensation for the iter26-S1 FNP re-land. After folding FNP into durability, opponent AI correctly diverted fire from FNP-bearing defenders to no-FNP horde armies (Orks regressed +5.7 -> +10.1 at N=20). Real play: a 10-model Boyz squad still threatens return fire after losing 4 models, because the defender allocates wounds per attack and the unit only ceases to be a threat when fully wiped. Modelling: multiply effective durability by (1.0 + max(0, sibling_count - 1) * 0.05) where sibling_count is alive same-name models in the defender's army.

simulator.first_turn_rolloff.quoted_text: The players roll off. The winner declares whether they will take the first or second turn.
simulator.first_turn_rolloff.trigger: Once per battle, during mission sequence step 12 (Determine First Turn), before the first battle round begins
simulator.first_turn_rolloff.effect: The player who wins the roll-off chooses whether to take the first or second turn; that turn order then persists for the entire battle — the same player always takes the first turn in every subsequent battle round

simulator.tank_shock_dice.rule_name: Tank Shock (dice-faithful ON path, gate SWEG_TANKSHOCK_DICE)
simulator.tank_shock_dice.quoted_text: WHEN: Your Charge phase, just after a VEHICLE unit from your army ends a Charge move. TARGET: That VEHICLE unit. EFFECT: Select one enemy unit within Engagement Range of your unit, and select one VEHICLE model in your unit that is within Engagement Range of that enemy unit. Roll a number of D6 equal to the Toughness characteristic of the selected VEHICLE model. For each 5+, that enemy unit suffers 1 mortal wound (to a maximum of 6 mortal wounds).
simulator.tank_shock_dice.trigger: ON path (SWEG_TANKSHOCK_DICE=1) only; charge phase, after a friendly VEHICLE unit ends a successful charge move and the stratagem fires; same trigger as Stratagem.Tank Shock
simulator.tank_shock_dice.effect: Roll a number of D6 equal to the charging VEHICLE model's Toughness characteristic (charger.profile.toughness); each die of 5 or 6 adds 1 mortal wound, capped at 6 total, applied via _apply_mortal_wounds. OFF path (default): flat 2 mortal wounds (the incumbent deterministic approximation, byte-identical to prior behaviour, no additional random draws).
